narrationScript: After C, Python offers a fresh perspective. It abstracts away low-level details, letting us focus on problem-solving. This isn't about one language being 'better,' but about using the right tool. Python emphasizes readability, with its unique use of indentation to define code blocks, unlike C's curly braces. This 'Pythonic way' promotes clean, maintainable code. Indentation is critical: four spaces per level is standard. Mixing tabs and spaces can cause `IndentationError`s, so be consistent! Comments start with a `#` symbol, ignored by the interpreter, but invaluable for notes. Variables in Python are dynamically typed; you don't declare types explicitly. `x = 10` makes `x` an integer, `name = 'Alice'` makes `name` a string. Python infers the type at runtime. While flexible, it's wise to keep track of a variable's type to avoid errors.
